chapter: Wider talk: bands, places and players
title: Charlie Johnson's band at Smalls Paradise, and Sidney De Paris
summary: He remembers the solid drumming of George Stafford and cornetist Sidney De Paris in New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. You reminded me of something when you mentioned Jabba. Did they have a band at Smalls Paradise, or just a piano player, or what?
Well, Charlie Johnson was the piano player.

And that was the band, Charlie Johnson's band. Yeah. And they had the, they weren't one of the greatest drummers there, uh, George Stafford. Mm-hmm. And his sister, his sister was singing in a chorus there, see. And he just, he just had a good, solid beat. Mm-hmm. All these other guys, they all want to be funny guys, and turn sticks around and be a fancy drummer. Yeah. And they're not the drums and stuff, what they're supposed to be playing. Mm-hmm. You see what I mean? And I used to go down there because I enjoyed the sound of the band and the beat that they had. They had the, uh, uh, uh, oh, what the hell was his name? Wilbur and his brother playing in the band. Sidney? Huh? Sidney? Sidney. Sidney was playing, was playing cornette in the band, see.
And, uh, later on, we played, uh, with that picture I showed you, of Don Redmond's band. He played at the, uh, Casino Dupree in New York.
With that band, see. Then, then, then he played along, 52nd Street and all.
That's, that's who I'm talking about. Nothing about, but I'm talking about.
Oh, yeah. I get names all mixed up. Yeah, well, I used to go to Ryan's and hear them.

Yeah, well, that's what I said. Sidney De Parry. Two brothers, three stars, yeah. Uh, bands like that, I mean, we used to go there because they played the kind of music that we played. I mean, uh, I mean, the, the style that, uh, that we liked. You know.
